A *vernissage* is the opening of an exhibition, when the works are hung and
shown at their best. This package **prepares** clinical cohort data and
**shows** them: publication-ready figures with a common theme and
colour-blind safe palettes, and polished `gt` tables.

Data are in wide format: one row per subject, one column per variable and
visit (`NFL_V0`, `NFL_V3`). Columns can be given as strings, bare names or
tidyselect helpers.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Clement-Poupelin/vernissage")

# optional features
install.packages(c("gt", "car", "DT", "ggrepel", "nortest", "stringi"))
```

## What it does

| Family | Main functions | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Import | `read_cohort_csv()`, `clean_colnames()`, `rename_with_map()`, `catalog_vars()` | French CSV exports (`;`, `,` decimals, Latin-1), clean names, variable catalogue |
| Visits | `visit_to_long()`, `visit_add_deltas()`, `visit_map_suffix()`, `combine_bilateral()` | long format, changes between visits, left / right means |
| Outliers | `outlier_detect()`, `outlier_mask()`, `outlier_flag_mad()`, `outlier_flag_iqr()` | modified z-score and Tukey fences, documented and referenced |
| Transformations | `transform_compare()`, `transform_choose()`, `transform_apply()`, `transform_boxcox()` | log / Box-Cox decided at baseline, applied at follow-up |
| Description | `describe_cohort()`, `describe_normality()`, `na_summary()`, `cor_matrix_test()`, `pca_compute()` | cohort overview table, normality, missing data, correlations, PCA |
| Figures | `plot_distribution()`, `plot_na_map()`, `plot_paired_visits()`, `plot_trajectories()`, `plot_cor_heatmap()`, `plot_pca_*()`, `plot_radar()`, `plot_forest()` | one function per figure of a cohort report |
| Style | `theme_pub()`, `pal_levels()`, `fmt_p()`, `label_expand()` | publication theme, Okabe-Ito palette, p-value and label formatting |
| Reports | `gt_pub()`, `gt_signif()`, `qmd_tabset()`, `qmd_callout_raw()` | `gt` tables with significance highlighting, Quarto tabsets and callouts |

## Example

```r
library(vernissage)

# the cohort at a glance
describe_cohort(cohort_sim, vars = c(AGE, SEX, BMI, NFL_V0, MOCA_V0, FALL_V0),
                by = GROUP, id_col = ID)
plot_na_map(cohort_sim, vars = c(NFL_V0:CRP_V3), id_col = ID)

# distributions with outliers and group tests
plot_distribution(cohort_sim, c(NFL_V0, MOCA_V0, SEX), group = GROUP, outlier_mad = TRUE)

# how each subject moves between visits
plot_paired_visits(cohort_sim, c(NFL_V0, MOCA_V0), id_col = ID, transitions = TRUE)

# group profiles
plot_radar(cohort_sim, c(AGE, BMI, NFL_V0, IL6_V0, MOCA_V0, UPDRS_V0, SEX),
           group = GROUP, normalize = "zscore", quali_levels = list(SEX = "Female"))
```

The rendered figures are in the articles of the documentation:
[Describing a cohort](https://clement-poupelin.github.io/vernissage/articles/describing.html),
[Figures](https://clement-poupelin.github.io/vernissage/articles/figures.html),
[Preprocessing](https://clement-poupelin.github.io/vernissage/articles/preprocessing.html)
and [Tables and Quarto reports](https://clement-poupelin.github.io/vernissage/articles/reporting.html).

## Companion package

[lodestar](https://github.com/Clement-Poupelin/lodestar) handles limits of
detection and cut-offs (median split, tertiles, reclassification between visits).
